description: AETHER  is a team dedicated to advancing astronaut safety and healthcare through innovative technology. We aim to develop intelligent health monitoring solutions that track astronaut vital signs, detect potential health risks, and enable real-time communication between astronauts, medical professionals, and mission control. Our mission is to make space exploration safer, smarter, and more sustainable by putting astronaut well-being at the center of every mission.

details:
ASTRA-360: Adaptive Spaceflight Tracking, Risk Intelligence & Autonomous Health Assistant

Tagline: Your Health. Your Mission. Your Intelligence.

1. What does your project do and how does it work?

ASTRA-360 is an integrated astronaut health-monitoring and decision-support platform designed to support crew health during long-duration space missions. It brings together personal health monitoring, mission environmental awareness and AI-assisted medical guidance in one unified system.

The platform combines three interconnected components: ASTRA, which monitors an astronaut's personal health; ORBIT, which tracks mission environmental conditions and spaceflight hazards; and PULSE, an AI-assisted medical companion that helps astronauts understand their health information and receive appropriate guidance.

ASTRA collects and organizes health indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, blood glucose, sleep duration, mood, fatigue and reported symptoms. It compares available measurements against the astronaut's personal baseline to identify meaningful changes and trends.

ORBIT monitors relevant mission-environment information, including radiation readings, oxygen, CO2 and temperature. It also addresses NASA's five major human spaceflight hazards: radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity and hostile or closed environments.

At the core of the platform is the Mission Health Correlation Engine (MHCE), which combines health history, symptoms, personal baselines and environmental records to identify potentially concerning patterns. Rather than treating each measurement independently, it provides explainable observations and highlights possible relationships between mission conditions and health changes.

PULSE provides a conversational interface and guided symptom-assessment workflow. It translates complex information into understandable explanations, offers appropriate monitoring and preventive guidance, and identifies when medical personnel should be contacted. A rules-based safety mechanism prioritizes urgent escalation over AI-generated responses.

ASTRA-360 also includes an interactive Digital Health Twin, predictive health analytics, a prevention and recovery planner, a medical knowledge library and a Mission Health Brief that summarizes the astronaut's health, environmental conditions, important observations and recommended next steps in simple language.

The platform is designed with offline functionality in mind, using cached educational information and deterministic assessment rules when cloud-based AI services are unavailable.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Continuous health awareness: Organizes multiple health indicators and historical measurements in one place.
  • Personalized monitoring: Compares measurements with individual health baselines rather than relying only on generic reference values.
  • Early identification of concerning patterns: Highlights combinations of changes, such as reduced sleep, increasing resting heart rate and repeated fatigue, for further assessment.
  • Environmental awareness: Connects astronaut health monitoring with relevant mission environmental information and spaceflight hazards.
  • Accessible medical information: Makes complex health measurements and scientific information easier for astronauts to understand.
  • AI-assisted support: Provides guided symptom assessment and understandable explanations without replacing qualified medical professionals.
  • Explainable recommendations: Shows why an observation matters and what monitoring or follow-up action may be appropriate.
  • Offline resilience: Supports access to cached information and rules-based functionality when connectivity is limited.
  • Organized health records: Maintains assessment history and tracks preventive actions and reassessments.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact of ASTRA-360 is to contribute to safer, more informed and proactive astronaut health monitoring, particularly during long-duration missions where distance from Earth, communication delays and limited immediate medical assistance create additional challenges.

By bringing personal health information, environmental observations and medical guidance together, ASTRA-360 aims to help astronauts recognize changes in their health patterns, understand potential concerns and communicate relevant information to mission medical teams.

The platform also aims to reduce the complexity of interpreting multiple health indicators by converting them into concise, understandable and actionable summaries.

In the longer term, ASTRA-360 could serve as a conceptual foundation for integrated astronaut health-support systems for future lunar and Mars missions, where independent health awareness and reliable decision support will be increasingly important.

Its broader significance lies in demonstrating how AI, data analytics and human-centred software design can contribute to healthcare in challenging and resource-constrained environments.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware or software did you use?

ASTRA-360 is designed as a modular full-stack software platform.

Frontend and user interface

  • React and TypeScript for the interactive application.
  • Vite for frontend development and building.
  • Tailwind CSS for styling and responsive layouts.
  • React Router for navigation.
  • Recharts for health and environmental data visualization.
  • Three.js / React Three Fiber for the interactive Digital Health Twin.
  • Lucide for interface icons.

Backend and data management

  • Python for backend logic.
  • FastAPI for REST API development.
  • Pydantic for data validation.
  • SQLite for structured data storage.

Artificial intelligence and analytics

  • Gemini API for AI-assisted PULSE conversations and natural-language health summaries, accessed through the backend.
  • Rules-based assessment logic for transparent health observations and escalation.
  • Baseline comparison and trend-analysis algorithms.
  • Mission Health Correlation Engine for examining relationships between health and environmental records.

Offline functionality

  • Progressive Web App (PWA) architecture.
  • IndexedDB for local data storage.
  • Service workers and cached medical information for offline access.

Development environment

  • Google Antigravity as the AI-assisted development environment.
  • Git and GitHub for version control and collaboration.

The initial prototype uses software-based data inputs and simulated mission scenarios. It does not claim integration with actual NASA or CSA medical sensors or spacecraft hardware. Future hardware integration is a potential extension.

5. How is your project creative?

ASTRA-360's creativity lies in combining several traditionally separate astronaut-health support functions into one connected and explainable platform.

Instead of displaying isolated measurements, it creates a broader picture of astronaut health by bringing together personal baselines, health trends, reported symptoms and mission environmental observations.

Its most distinctive innovations include:

  1. Mission Health Correlation Engine: Connects health indicators and mission environmental records to highlight potentially meaningful patterns rather than examining readings independently.
  2. Interactive Digital Health Twin: Provides a visual representation of the astronaut's health systems, allowing users to explore relevant body regions, measurements and assessment findings.
  3. PULSE Medical Companion: Converts complex health information into accessible explanations through conversational and guided assessment workflows.
  4. Mission Health Brief: Transforms detailed assessment results into a short, personalized report explaining the astronaut's current observations, relevant environmental conditions, recommended actions and the reasons behind them.
  5. Autonomous Action and Recovery: Goes beyond identifying observations by helping astronauts track recommended monitoring actions, complete them and reassess their condition.
  6. Offline-aware architecture: Recognizes the communication limitations of deep-space missions and provides a rules-based fallback with cached educational resources when cloud AI is unavailable.

The combination creates a unified health-awareness experience rather than another conventional dashboard or chatbot.

6. What factors did your team consider?

Our team considered the scientific, operational, technical and human factors associated with monitoring astronaut health during space missions.

Scientific and health considerations

  • NASA's five major human spaceflight hazards.
  • Physiological and behavioural changes associated with long-duration spaceflight.
  • The importance of individual health baselines.
  • The need to interpret multiple indicators together.
  • The distinction between observed associations and proven causes.
  • The limitations of simulated measurements and unvalidated predictive models.

Mission and operational considerations

  • Limited and delayed communication with Earth.
  • Restricted access to immediate medical assistance.
  • The importance of clear and timely health information.
  • The need for offline access to essential educational information.
  • The importance of escalating serious concerns to qualified medical personnel.

Human-centred design considerations

  • Simple language understandable without medical expertise.
  • Clear and accessible visualizations.
  • Minimal cognitive load during demanding mission activities.
  • Concise health summaries and actionable recommendations.
  • A calm, readable interface that distinguishes routine information from urgent warnings.

Technical considerations

  • Modular and scalable architecture.
  • Secure handling of API keys and health information.
  • Reliable data validation and storage.
  • Consistent integration between frontend and backend.
  • Graceful handling of missing data and AI service failures.
  • Transparent and explainable rules-based assessment.

Ethical and safety considerations

  • AI must assist rather than replace medical professionals.
  • Urgent escalation must not depend on an LLM.
  • No unsupported diagnoses or medication prescriptions.
  • Uncertainty and missing information must be communicated clearly.
  • Simulated data must be distinguished from actual measurements.
  • Recommendations must not override mission medical protocols.

Through these considerations, our team aims to build a solution that is not only innovative and visually engaging, but also responsible, understandable and relevant to the real challenges of human space exploration.

ASTRA-360 represents our vision of a more connected, proactive and astronaut-centred approach to health awareness in space.
